Expectation1: Support each other emotionally during tough times
Situation1: One sibling is preparing for a stressful final exam and is feeling anxious about the outcome.
Situation2: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Story: I sat at my desk, textbooks spread out, but my mind was far from the pages. My younger brother was pacing the hallway, muttering formulas under his breath, his anxiety almost tangible. I knew he needed me—he always counted on me to calm him down before big exams. But just as I was about to go to him, my phone buzzed. It was a message from my best friend, short and cold. She’d misunderstood my last text, and now she thought I was upset with her. She wanted to talk, right now, to clear things up. I could hear my brother’s shaky breathing from the next room, and I could feel my friend’s hurt through the screen. Both needed me, both expected me to be there, but I only had one self to give. My heart pounded as I stared at my phone, torn between the two people who mattered most.
